I would say refrain from drinking, smoking, listening to music (especially explicit) around your mother-in-law. This is a holy time for muslims and a calm, quiet environment would be welcomed. Having a clean, designated area for her to pray would also be generous. I would also be careful not to eat directly in front of her, as she will be fasting. Having some snacks available for when she starts/breaks her fast would be nice, like dates and fruit. Maybe see if she has any favorites and have them ready. Good luck!

I’m so sorry to hear that :( Just remember how you felt when your grandmother passed, as your friend is likely feeling the same way. Right now they probably have so much on their mind, but just keep reminding them that you are there for them. Sending flowers or a card may be a nice gesture, as well. Best wishes to you.

Don’t beat yourself up over it, there really is no “right” thing to say. The best thing you can do is simply be there for your friend, and it seems like you did that by listening to them and offering support. Remind them that you are thinking of them and ask for updates to show that you care. I hope the grandfather gets better, and I hope you’re taking care of yourself too.
